title: Next.js vs WordPress for a Business Website
verdict: Choose WordPress when marketing must change layouts often without developers and budget is tight. Choose Next.js when speed, security and custom features such as calculators, portals or integrations matter.
seoTitle: Next.js vs WordPress for Business Websites
seoDescription: Next.js or WordPress for a business website: speed, SEO, security, editing experience, plugins, hosting and the cost of maintenance.
summary: WordPress powers a large share of websites and lets non-technical teams edit pages easily with themes and plugins, but needs regular updates and can slow down with plugins. Next.js is a modern framework that produces very fast, secure sites, usually paired with a headless CMS for editing, and needs developers for structural changes.

dataPoints.label: Speed
dataPoints.value: Next.js sites are typically faster out of the box; WordPress depends on theme and plugins

dataPoints.label: Editing
dataPoints.value: WordPress: built in. Next.js: through a headless CMS

dataPoints.label: Security
dataPoints.value: WordPress needs constant plugin and core updates; Next.js has a smaller attack surface

dataPoints.label: Custom features
dataPoints.value: Easier in Next.js; WordPress relies on plugins or custom PHP

dataPoints.label: Hosting
dataPoints.value: WordPress: PHP hosting. Next.js: Vercel or similar platforms

body:
## SEO

Both can rank well. Speed and [Core Web Vitals](/glossary/core-web-vitals), structured content and good writing matter more than the platform.

See [Next.js vs WordPress in 2026](/blog/nextjs-vs-wordpress-for-a-business-website-in-2026) and the [headless CMS entry](/glossary/headless-cms).

Prices and features change often; check current details before deciding.

faqs.q: Can we move from WordPress to Next.js?
faqs.a: Yes. Content migrates and URL redirects protect rankings.
The software is free; themes, plugins, hosting and maintenance are not.
